We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to construct route using templates.

We have one template (851565) that seems to disconnection of an amide with a trans-alkene attached to aromatic ring (C= C). The template: [#7:3]-[C:2](=[O])/[CH]=[CH]/[c] >> O-C(=O)-CH2- C(=O)-N etc. Actually retro: product is amide with trans-alkene attached to aromatic ring. The retro template splits into a carboxylic acid (O-C(=O)-CH2-?) and a methyl aryl? Let's examine: canonical: O-C(=O)-[CH2]-[C](=O)-N? Wait.

The template: O-C(=O)-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[#7:3])=[O;D1;H0:4].[CH3;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]>>[#7:3]-[C:2](=[O;D1;H0:4])/[CH;D2;+0:1]=[CH;D2;+0:5]/[c:6]

So product: amide with trans-alkene linking to aromatic ring (c). The precursors: a carboxylic acid (O-C(=O)-CH2- C(=O)-? Actually O-C(=O)-CH2-? Wait: O-C(=O)-CH2-? The fragment is O-C(=O)-CH2-? The [C:2] is carbonyl carbon attached to N (amide). The precursor is a carboxylic acid (O-C(=O)-CH2-?) plus a methyl aryl (CH3 attached to aromatic). So the disconnection is amide formation between an aniline (or amine) and an acid? Actually product has N attached to carbonyl (amide). The template splits into a carboxylic acid (O-C(=O)-CH2-?) and a methyl aryl (CH3-aryl). The CH3-aryl is the alkene side? Wait the [CH3]-[c] is the alkene carbon (CH3 attached to alkene). So the product's alkene is formed from condensation of a carboxylic acid with a methyl aryl? This seems like a Knoevenagel condensation? Actually O-C(=O)-CH2- is a malonate? Not.

Nevertheless, we can use this template to disconnect the trans-alkene amide part.

Our target: aromatic sulfonamide attached to another aromatic ring bearing trans-alkene amide side chain.

We can think of retrosynthesis:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and an aniline. So we can get two fragments: 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) and 4-(trans-... amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring (the left phenyl). So we can disconnect to give the left phenyl amine (p-toluidine) and the sulfonyl chloride derived from the right phenyl sulfonyl chloride (p-(trans-... amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride). Then we can form sulfonamide via sulfonyl chloride + amine.

Thus step 1: sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine -> target.

Now we need to get sulfonyl chloride precursor: aromatic sulfonyl chloride with the trans-alkene amide substituent on the ring.

We can disconnect the amide side chain using template 851565: the amide attached to aromatic ring (the right phenyl) with trans-alkene linking to an anilide (C= C - C(=O)N- phenyl). The template splits into a carboxylic acid (maybe cinnamic acid derivative) and a methyl aryl (maybe to form the alkene). Actually product: .../C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-N? Wait the product side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (an anilide with an aniline attached to carbonyl). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (aniline) which also has an NH (aniline). So the amide is N-aryl (anilide) with an ortho? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH at para? It's an aniline with an amino group (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an amino substituent (aniline). So the amide is formed from aniline (aniline with NH2) reacting with a cinnamic acid derivative (trans-phenylacrylic acid). So the template likely splits into cinnamic acid (O-C(=O)-CH=CH-Ph) and an aniline (NH2-Ph). Indeed the template's precursors: O-C(=O)-CH2-? Wait but the template shows O-C(=O)-CH2-? Actually O-C(=O)-CH2-? The [CH2] is the carbon adjacent to carbonyl, not the alkene carbon. But maybe the mapping is off.

Nevertheless, we can propose step 2: disconnection of amide: produce trans-cinnamic acid (or 4-(sulfonyl)cinnamic acid) and an aniline (p-aminophenyl). The amide formation is standard.

Thus overall route:

Target -> (step1) sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine (commercial) -> target (sulfonamide formation).

Sulfonyl chloride precursor: 4-(trans-... amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride.

Step2: from that sulfonyl chloride, disconnect amide: produce trans-cinnamic acid derivative (4-(sulfonyl)cinnamic acid) and an aniline (p-aminophenyl). Then amide formation yields sulfonyl chloride with amide side chain.

Step3: The trans-cinnamic acid derivative can be obtained from commercially available 4-bromobenzaldehyde via Wittig? But we need max 3 steps total, so we need to have sulfonyl chloride already containing the amide side chain, maybe we can get it directly via sulfonylation of a commercially available sulfonyl chloride with the aniline after amide formation? Wait order: we could first form amide on right phenyl, then sulfonylate with left phenyl amine. That is 2 steps.

Thus we need commercially available right phenyl sulfonyl chloride (p-sulfonyl chloride) with the trans-alkene amide already attached. Is that commercially available? Likely not.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation of left phenyl amine with sulfonyl chloride derived from right phenyl sulfonic acid (which could be made from sulfonation of right phenyl). But that adds steps.

Maybe we can reverse: first form sulfonamide between p-toluidine and 4-aminophenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to right phenyl which also has amide side chain. Could we first form sulfonamide using 4-aminophenyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) and p-toluidine? That would give sulfonamide linking two phenyls, but we still need amide side chain on right phenyl. Then we can do amide formation on that right phenyl (which already has sulfonamide). That would be 2 steps as well.

Thus we need commercially available 4-aminophenyl sulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride). Is that available? Likely yes (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride). Then step1: sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine -> sulfonamide linking two phenyls (product: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-p-aminophenyl). This intermediate has an aniline group on the right phenyl (NH2). Step2: acylate that aniline with trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) to form amide (C=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait the target amide is attached to the right phenyl via carbonyl to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The right phenyl has an amide attached to its para position? Actually the SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the right phenyl (c2) has a para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-N (anilide). So the amide nitrogen is attached to another phenyl (c3) which also has an NH (aniline). So the right phenyl has a side chain: trans-alkene attached to carbonyl attached to an aniline (which also has an NH2). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 (para?). Actually Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an amino group at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino at position 1 and another amino at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amino at both ends? It is a phenyl with two amino groups at positions 1 and (maybe 4). The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That's a phenyl with two amino substituents at positions 1 and 6? Actually both at the same carbon? Not possible. The SMILES indicates an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) and there is another N attached to the aromatic carbon at the other end (position 6). So it's a 1,4-diaminobenzene (p-phenylenediamine) attached via one NH to carbonyl. So the amide is formed from p-phenylenediamine (one NH used for amide, the other remains free). So the amide precursor is p-phenylenediamine (commercial) and trans-cinnamic acid (or its derivative) to give the amide side chain.

Thus route:

Step1: Sulfonylation: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) + 4-(sulfonyl chloride) phenyl? Wait we need sulfonyl chloride attached to right phenyl which also will later be functionalized with amide. Could start with 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride then later substitute bromine with amide side chain via Suzuki? That adds steps.

Better: Use p-toluidine + 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide linking p-tolyl-sulfonyl-p-aminophenyl. This intermediate has a free amine (the second NH) on the right phenyl (p-phenylenediamine). Then step2: acylate that free amine with trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) to give the amide side chain. This yields final product (since the amide attaches to the same phenyl, leaving the other NH free). Indeed final product has the right phenyl with amide attached to one NH and the other NH free (the N attached to carbonyl is part of amide, the other N is free). In SMILES, the right phenyl has "Nc3ccccc3N": the first N is attached to carbonyl (amide), the second N is free (attached to aromatic). So our intermediate after sulfonamide formation has both NHs free (p-phenylenediamine). After acylation, one NH becomes amide, the other remains free. So that matches.

Thus we need reagents:

- p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) – commercially available, cheap.
- 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride) – commercially available.
- trans-cinnamic acid (3-phenyl-2-propenoic acid) – commercially available.
- Possibly coupling agent (e.g., DCC) but not needed as we just need to list precursors; we can assume amide formation via standard coupling.

We need to ensure total price <= $9999. Likely each is cheap (<$200). So fine.

Now we need to construct JSON route with up to 3 steps. Steps are reactions with template IDs.

We have template for sulfonamide formation? Need to find a template for sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. Let's search.
